Admission ties a seat to one pigment lot from a mill fed by a glacier, whose soft melt fixes colour. The applicant sends a velvet swatch dyed from that lot; a lab reports its reflectance curve from 400 to 700 nm and the node hashes it against the mill's invoice number. Lot ids run in series, so fifty seats bought at once read as one buyer. One lot, one seat.

A velvet nap hides a smudge flat cloth shows, though the spectrometer reads the pile flat. Dye 12 dollars, bench 55, courier 18: a cloned cohort clears near 4,250 dollars and leaves 50 consecutive lot numbers over one address.
